Subject: Week of Nov 1 — Exec action log + QBR risk heatmap

Morning — sending this week’s concise exec packet: wins, highest-priority risks for the QBR, and the actions we’ve committed to. Kept it short so this can be forwarded into decks.

Wins
- Hosted: 10% reduction in median gen latency after kernel tuning (prod canary passed).
- Dedicated: first customer on Reserved capacity migration completed (BrightScale pilot).
- Optimize: initial quantization profiles show ~2.4x token-cost improvement on internal test bench.

Top risks (QBR impact lane)
1) Capacity: Reserved pools may not meet peak slot concurrency for two enterprise customers during the QBR demo window (see SUP-3421). Likelihood: medium-high. Impact: demo failure / SLA hit.
2) Data path: Audit log retention gap for Private deployments — infra has a short-term coverage plan but we need formal verification for the SOC-2 evidence bundle. Likelihood: medium.
3) Model regressions: recent model v2.1 rollout produced higher hallucination rate on a targeted eval set; hold for canary rollback if thresholds crossed. Likelihood: low-medium.

Asks (what I need from this distro)
- Laura: can you surface an SLA contingency slide for the QBR pack by EOD Monday? (one bullet on fallback routing + customer-facing messaging).
- Karthik / Jonas: please confirm capacity mitigation ETA and any customer-impacting limits (Karthik, link to SUP-3421).
- Marissa: want you to own outreach to BrightScale on migration timeline / exec alignment — cc’d Brian for transparency.

Attachments: qbr_risk-heatmap_v1.pdf (heatmap + one-line mitigations), exec_action_log.csv (action owners + due dates).

If no objections, I’ll fold approvals into the QBR pack we’re sending to runs-on Monday 11/9.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
VP, Operations
Redwood Inference

Quick capacity update:
- Root cause: burst concurrency on reserved pools combined with suboptimal pre-warming for the demo model variant.
- Short-term mitigation (today -> demo): increase reserved pre-warm to +20% for the demo window; throttle background organic test traffic during the window.
- Longer-term (next 2 weeks): we have a config change to pool-sizing logic (SUP-3421). ETA: config patch by 11/10, verification by 11/12.

Expected customer-visible impact for short-term approach: ~150-300ms added tail latency on heavy requests, test OK on internal load.

Link to ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-3421

Karthik
VP, Serving Runtime
